title: Average Basket Size per Customer
description:
For each customer, compute the **average number of distinct products per order** (basket size). Join customers to their orders and line items.

**Tables:** `customers` (`id`, `name`), `orders` (`id`, `customer_id`), `order_items` (`order_id`, `product_id`)

Output columns: `customer_id`, `name`, `avg_basket_size`. Order by `customer_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice'),(2,'Bob'),(3,'Carol'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1),(2,1),(3,2),(4,3),(5,3); CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INT, product_id INT); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,10),(1,11),(1,12),(2,10),(3,20),(3,21),(4,10),(4,11),(4,12),(4,13),(5,20),(5,21);
solution_sql: SELECT c.id AS customer_id, c.name, ROUND(AVG(t.cnt)::NUMERIC, 2) AS avg_basket_size FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN (SELECT order_id, COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS cnt FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) t ON t.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY c.id
hints: First count DISTINCT product_id per order_id in a derived table.
Join that to customers via orders, then AVG the per-order counts.
explanation: Order 1 has 3 products, order 2 has 1 (Alice average 2). Order 3 has 2 (Bob average 2). Orders 4 and 5 have 4 and 2 (Carol average 3). Averaging distinct SKUs per order is the standard basket-size metric.
